BURSEVI:v10p253/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p253/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p253/r6.claim: Tamma means to rise over and overwhelm; al-kubra describes greatness, not old age. The event is the overwhelming Resurrection or second blast, arriving soon after the temporary worldly provision.
BURSEVI:v10p253/r6.anchor: كل شيء كثر حتى علا وغلب فقد طم من باب رد والكبرى تأنيث الأكبر من كبر بالضم بمعنى عظم

BURSEVI:v10p253/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p253/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p253/r7.claim: The surahs’ use of al-tamma and al-sakhkha suits their order: if tamma is the first blast, it precedes the deafening second blast; if it is the second, both descriptions fit.
BURSEVI:v10p253/r7.anchor: بمعنى النفخة الأولى للإهلاك فهو قبل الصح

QASHANI:79:34-41/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:79:34-41/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:79:34-41/r1.claim: The great calamity is the light of divine unity manifesting and effacing everything.
QASHANI:79:34-41/r1.anchor: تجلى نور الوحدة الذاتية الذي يطم على كل شيء فيطمسه ويمحوه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r3.claim: The passage contrasts the rebellious and disobedient people’s fate with glad tidings for those who feared God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r3.anchor: A mention of the fate of the rebellious and the disobedient on the Day of Judgement.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r1.claim: The passage turns from worldly livelihood to the afterlife; some take the fāʾ to indicate sequence, reinforced by the preceding word for provision.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r1.anchor: شروع في بيان معادهم أثر بيان أحوال معاشهم بقوله عز وجل متاعا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r2.claim: Ṭāmma comes from the idea of rising over something: the Great Overwhelming Calamity dominates all other calamities.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r2.anchor: والطامة أعظم الدواهي لأنه من طم بمعنى علا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r3.claim: Its description as great may reinforce its severity, distinguish it from known worldly disasters, or mark it as greater than every calamity.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r3.anchor: قيل فوصفها بالكبرى للتأكيد ولو فسر كونها طامة بكونها غالبة للخلائق

ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that الطامة الكبرى is a name for the Resurrection, and also identifies it as the second trumpet blast.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r4.anchor: وروي كونها اسما من أسمائها هنا عن ابن عباس وعنه أيضا وعن الحسن أنها النفخة الثانية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r5.speaker: القاسم بن الوليد الهمداني
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r5.claim: Al-Qasim ibn al-Walid al-Hamdani says it is the hour when the people of Paradise are led to Paradise and the people of the Fire to the Fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r5.anchor: عن القاسم بن الوليد الهمداني أنها الساعة التي يساق فيها أهل الجنة إلى الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r6.speaker: عمرو بن قيس الكندي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r6.claim: Amr ibn Qays al-Kindi narrows it to the hour when the people of Hell are driven into the Fire; Mujahid says it is their presentation to Malik.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p35#2/r6.anchor: عن عمرو بن قيس الكندي أنها ساعة يساق أهل النار إلى النار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r1.claim: The overwhelming calamity is the second blast, when Resurrection begins; it is called overwhelming because it engulfs every other terror, and Arabs use the term for an unbearable disaster.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p330/r1.anchor: يعني النفخة الثانية التي فيها البعث وقامت القيامة، وسميت القيامة: "طامة" لأنها تطم على كل هائلة

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:32-36/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:32-36/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:32-36/r3.claim: The overwhelming catastrophe is the greatest disaster: the Resurrection, the second blast, or the hour when the saved and damned are led to their destinations.
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:32-36/r3.anchor: { فإذا جاءت الطامة } الداهية التي تطم أي تعلو على سائر الدواهي

BINTSHATI:v1p154/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r1.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r1.claim: Al-Raghib identifies al-tamma al-kubra as the Resurrection; Ibn Abbas says it is the second trumpet blast, while Mujahid says it is when the two groups are driven toward their destinations.
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r1.anchor: وهي النفخة الثانية فيما روي عن "ابن عباس" أو وقت سوق أهل الجنة إليها

BINTSHATI:v1p154/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari lists all three interpretations and appears to prefer the Resurrection; the word occurs nowhere else in the Qur'an.
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r2.anchor: وجاء الزمخشري في الكشاف بهذه الأقوال الثلاثة متتالية

BINTSHATI:v1p154/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r3.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI:v1p154/r3.claim: Al-Raghib derives tamma from an overflowing sea; Arabic also uses al-tamma for an overwhelming calamity, which supports al-Zamakhshari's interpretation as Resurrection.

NAHHAS:v5p146/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p146/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p146/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Great Overwhelming is the Resurrection, magnified and warned about by God.
NAHHAS:v5p146/r3.anchor: روى ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس قال القيامة عظم الله أمرها وحذر منه

NAHHAS:v5p146/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p146/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p146/r4.claim: Arabs call anything momentous a ṭāmmah.
NAHHAS:v5p146/r4.anchor: العرب إذا عظمت الشيء وصفته بالطامة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p318/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p318/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v8p318/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses al-ṭāmmah al-kubrā as the overwhelming, supreme calamity.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p318/r7.anchor: أي الداهية الدهياء التي تطم أي تعلو

BIQAI-FULL:v8p318/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p318/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p318/r8.claim: The apodosis of idhā is omitted and understood as people being divided into the wretched and the blessed.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p318/r8.anchor: والعامل في ( إذا ) محذوف تقديره : فصل الناس إلى شقي وسعيد

DURR-FULL:v8p412/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p412/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p412/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says al-tammah al-kubra is one of the names of the Resurrection Day.

DURR-FULL:v8p412/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p412/r8.speaker: القاسم بن الوليد الهمذاني
DURR-FULL:v8p412/r8.claim: Al-Qasim ibn al-Walid says the great calamity is when the people of Paradise are driven to Paradise and the people of Hell to Hell.
DURR-FULL:v8p412/r8.anchor: عن القاسم بن الوليد الهمذاني في قوله

DURR-FULL:v8p412/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p412/r9.speaker: عمرو بن قيس الكندي
DURR-FULL:v8p412/r9.claim: Amr ibn Qays says it is when the command comes to take someone to the Fire.

DURR-FULL:v8p412/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p412/r11.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p412/r11.claim: Mujahid says the great calamity is when people are sent to Malik, guardian of Hell; ṭaghā means disobeyed, marsāhā means its time, and its mention means the Hour.
DURR-FULL:v8p412/r11.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {فإذا جاءت الطامة}

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r4.claim: The warning and glad tidings follow the proof of resurrection because judgment follows resurrection; the wise prepare for lasting reward rather than transient pleasure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r4.anchor: فإن إثبات البعث يقتضي الجزاء إذ هو حكمته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r5.claim: The warning moves from the resurrection's first convulsion to the blast and then the Great Calamity, a term encompassing all horrors until each group reaches its abode.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r5.anchor: ثم بالزجرة ، وأخيرا بالطامة الكبرى لما في هذين الوصفين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r6.claim: The reminder of judgment follows the creation and provision of the earth because those worldly comforts end when resurrection and judgment arrive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r6.anchor: ومن تمام المناسبة للتذكير بيوم الجزاء وقوعه عقب التذكير بخلق الأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r7.claim: Alternatively, the Great Calamity branches from the single blast and is itself that blast.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p88/r7.anchor: على قوله : { فإنما هي زجرة واحدة فإذا هم بالساهرة }

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p23#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p23#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p23#4/r1.claim: Al-ṭāmma is a calamity that overwhelms everything else.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p23#4/r1.anchor: والطامة الحادثة التي تطم على ما سواها أي تعلو فوقه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p23#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p23#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p23#4/r2.claim: Three interpretations are given: the second blast that raises the dead; the call to Hell's people to enter it; or the procession sending each group to its destination.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p23#4/r2.anchor: وفي المراد بها هاهنا ثلاثة أقوال أحدها النفخة الثانية التي فيها البعث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r1.claim: The Great Overwhelming is Resurrection; it is so named because it overwhelms every dreadful matter, as another verse says the Hour is more grievous.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p317#2/r1.anchor: قاله ابن عباس، سميت بذلك لأنها تطم على كل أمر هائل مفظع،

JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r12.claim: Ṭāmma means an immense, overwhelming occurrence; it can describe what rises above and overcomes everything, or a calamity that cannot be repelled. The Resurrection is named for overpowering all else.
JISHUMI:v10p7271#2/r12.anchor: الطامة: الغاشية الغليظة، التي توفي كل شيء بالغلظ والكثرة

JISHUMI:v10p7275/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r1.claim: Other readings identify it as the second blast or the time when the people of Paradise and Hell are led to their destinations.
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r1.anchor: وقيل: الطامة النفخة الثانية، عن الحسن، وقيل: حين يساق أهل الجنة إلى الجنة

JISHUMI:v10p7275/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r2.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r2.claim: He interprets al-ṭāmma as the second blast.
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r2.anchor: وقيل: الطامة النفخة الثانية، عن الحسن

JISHUMI:v10p7275/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r3.claim: Another interpretation takes al-ṭāmma as the time when the people of Paradise are led to Paradise and the people of Hell to Hell.
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r3.anchor: وقيل: حين يساق أهل الجنة إلى الجنة، وأهل النار إلى النار

JISHUMI:v10p7275/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r12.claim: These verses also demonstrate the Resurrection's tremendous condition and many terrors.
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r12.anchor: وتدل على عظيم حال القيامة، وكثرة أهوالها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#2/r1.claim: الطامة is a calamity that overtops and overcomes every other calamity, as in the proverb about a river overrunning villages; it is the Resurrection because of its overwhelming force.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#2/r1.anchor: الطآمة } الداهية التي تطم على الدواهي ، أي : تعلو وتغلب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#2/r2.claim: Alternative identifications are the second trumpet blast or the moment the people of Paradise and Hell are driven to their destinations.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p698#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : هي النفخة الثانية . وقيل : الساعة التي تساق فيها أهل الجنة إلى الجنة وأهل النار إلى النار

SAMIN-DURR:79:34/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:34/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:34/r1.claim: One proposed answer to ‘idha ja’at’ is the following ‘fa-amma man tagha’, as in the example about Banu Tamim; another supplies an omitted answer meaning ‘the matter is so’.
SAMIN-DURR:79:34/r1.anchor: في جوابها أوجه، أحدها: قوله: " فأما من طغى " نحو: " إذا جاءك بنو تميم

SAMIN-DURR:79:34/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:34/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:79:34/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari supplies an omitted oath response, ‘if so, Hell is his abode’; other proposals say ‘they saw’ or ‘they knew’.
SAMIN-DURR:79:34/r2.anchor: فقدره الزمخشري: فإن الأمر كذلك، أي: فإن الجحيم مأواه

SAMIN-DURR:79:34/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:34/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:79:34/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa says the answer itself governs ‘idha’, whose meaning is expressed by ‘the day when the human remembers’.
SAMIN-DURR:79:34/r3.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " العامل فيها جوابها، وهو معنى قوله: " يوم يتذكر الإنسان

SAMIN-DURR:79:34/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:34/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:34/r4.claim: Al-tamma is a catastrophe that overtops other catastrophes in magnitude; its root also means burying or covering, as in the proverb about a flood covering villages.
SAMIN-DURR:79:34/r4.anchor: والطامة: الداهية تطم على غيرها من الدواهي لعظمها. والطم: الدفن

SAMIN-DURR:79:34/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:34/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:34/r5.claim: The ‘great catastrophe’ here is the second blast of the Trumpet, which brings about that overwhelming event.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r1.claim: The Greatest Overwhelming Event may be the second trumpet blast.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r2.speaker: الربيع
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r2.claim: It may be the Hour, which overwhelms every catastrophe and is more dreadful and bitter than any other.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r3.claim: It may be one of the names of the Resurrection.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r4.speaker: القاسم بن الوليد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r4.claim: It may refer to the moment the people of Paradise are led to Paradise and the people of the Fire to the Fire; this is also the meaning of Mujahid's view.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r4.anchor: إلى النار ، قاله القاسم بن الوليد ،

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r5.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r5.claim: In Arabic, ṭāmma can mean an event that covers, overwhelms, or terrifies because it covers everything.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r5.anchor: أحدها : الغاشية . الثاني : الغامرة . الثالث : الهائلة , ذكره ابن عيسى , لأنها تطم على كل شيء

MUQATIL:79:34-41/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:34-41/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:79:34-41/r1.claim: The Great Overwhelming Event is the final blast from Jerusalem, namely the Resurrection.
MUQATIL:79:34-41/r1.anchor: { فإذا جآءت الطآمة الكبرى } [آية: 34] يعني العظمى

MUQATIL:79:34-41/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:34-41/r3.speaker: شاهر همذان
MUQATIL:79:34-41/r3.claim: A poem attributed to Shahir of Hamadhan at Yarmuk uses the words al-sahirah and al-hafirah in a description of return after death, as lexical poetic evidence.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#12/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#12/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#12/r1.claim: The Great Calamity overwhelms and surpasses all calamities; it may be the second trumpet blast or the Hour when people are driven to their final abodes.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#12/r1.anchor: الداهية العظمى التى تطم على الدواهى أى تعلو وتغلب وهى النفخة الثانية

QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r1.speaker: ابن عباس عن الضحاك والحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas through al-Dahhak and Hasan say the Great Calamity is the second blast, which brings resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r1.anchor: النفخة الثانية، التي يكون معها البعث قاله ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r2.claim: Another report identifies it as the Resurrection, so named because its terror overwhelms everything else.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r2.anchor: أنها القيامة سميت بذلك لأنها تطم على كل شيء

QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r3.claim: The proverb “the valley ran and overwhelmed the villages” illustrates how the calamity overwhelms all else.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r4.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r4.claim: Al-Mubarrad says Arabs use tamma for an unbearable calamity, perhaps from a horse exhausting itself in a run or water filling a river.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r4.anchor: الطامة عند العرب الداهية التي لا تستطاع

QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r5.claim: Another derivation is from a flood that covers a well: tamma means to bury or rise over something.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r5.anchor: هي مأخوذة من طم السيل الركية أي دفنها

QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r6.speaker: القاسم بن الوليد الهمداني
QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r6.claim: Al-Qasim ibn al-Walid identifies the calamity as the moment Paradise’s people are led to Paradise and Hell’s people to Hell; Mujahid gives the same view.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r6.anchor: حين يساق أهل الجنة إلى الجنة وأهل النار إلى النار

QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r7.speaker: سفيان
QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r7.claim: Sufyan says it is the hour when the people of Hell are handed over to the guards.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:34/r7.anchor: هي الساعة التي يسلم فيها أهل النار إلى الزبانية

ZAJJAJ:v5p280#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p280#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p280#2/r5.claim: The Great Calamity is the blast that overwhelms everything and brings resurrection, judgment, punishment, torment, and mercy.
ZAJJAJ:v5p280#2/r5.anchor: إذا جاءت الصيحة التي تطم كل شيء، الصيحة التي يقع معها البعث والحساب والعقاب والعذاب والرحمة

RAZI-FULL:v31p46/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p46/r1.speaker: المبرد
RAZI-FULL:v31p46/r1.claim: Al-Mubarrad tentatively connects tamma to a horse exhausting itself in a run or water filling an entire river.
RAZI-FULL:v31p46/r1.anchor: قال المبرد : أخذت فيما أحسب من قولهم : طم الفرس طميما

RAZI-FULL:v31p46/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p46/r2.speaker: الليث
RAZI-FULL:v31p46/r2.claim: Al-Layth derives the root from filling a well with earth and burying it, and from a flood that covers a cistern.
RAZI-FULL:v31p46/r2.anchor: وقال الليث : الطم طم البئر بالتراب ، وهو الكبس

RAZI-FULL:v31p46/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p46/r3.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v31p46/r3.claim: Al-Qaffal says the root means burying and rising over; tamma is any great calamity that overwhelms and eclipses everything before it.
RAZI-FULL:v31p46/r3.anchor: قال القفال : أصل الطم الدفن والعلو ، وكل ما غلب شيئا وقهره وأخفاه فقد طمه

RAZI-FULL:v31p46#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p46#2/r1.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v31p46#2/r1.claim: Some identify the great catastrophe with Resurrection, whose fire, terrifying assembly and extraordinary signs eclipse every earlier terror.
RAZI-FULL:v31p46#2/r1.anchor: إنها يوم القيامة لأنه يشاهد فيه من النار

RAZI-FULL:v31p46#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p46#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v31p46#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan identifies it as the second blast, when all creatures are gathered for the Resurrection assembly.
RAZI-FULL:v31p46#2/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن : إنها هي النفخة الثانية التي عندها تحشر الخلائق إلى موقف القيامة

RAZI-FULL:v31p46#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p46#2/r3.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v31p46#2/r3.claim: Others identify the catastrophe with the time described by the next verses: perhaps the reading of each person's record, or the dispatch of people to Paradise and Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v31p46#2/r3.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون ذلك الوقت وقت قراءة الكتاب

STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r2.claim: It is titled from its first word and also called al-Sāhirah after the gathering plain and al-Ṭāmmah after the Great Calamity.
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r2.anchor: It is also known as al-Sāhirah

STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r9.claim: Verses 34–41 contrast believers' and disbelievers' outcomes on Resurrection Day.
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r9.anchor: returns to a description of the Day of Resurrection, contrasting the fate of the believers with that of the disbelievers

STUDYQURAN:79:34/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:34/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:34/r1.claim: Ṭāmmah derives from ṭamma, meaning abundant or rising over, like a flood; its overabundance encompasses everything.
STUDYQURAN:79:34/r1.anchor: derives from the verb ṭamma, meaning “to be abundant” or “to rise over,” as would a flood

STUDYQURAN:79:34/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:34/r2.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:79:34/r2.claim: Some identify the Great Calamity as the trumpet's second cry, gathering all humans and jinn.
STUDYQURAN:79:34/r2.anchor: Some take the Great Calamity as a reference to the second cry of the trumpet

STUDYQURAN:79:34/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:34/r3.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:79:34/r3.claim: Others identify it as Resurrection because it surpasses and predominates over all things.
STUDYQURAN:79:34/r3.anchor: others take it as a reference to the Resurrection, because it surpasses and predominates over

STUDYQURAN:79:34/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:34/r4.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:79:34/r4.claim: Some interpret the Calamity as the moment when Hell's people are led to Hell and Paradise's people to Paradise.
STUDYQURAN:79:34/r4.anchor: interpreted by some as a reference to the very moment when the people of Hell are led to Hell

STUDYQURAN:79:34/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:34/r5.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:79:34/r5.claim: Some understand the missing response to the conditional as affirming that the event must occur.
STUDYQURAN:79:34/r5.anchor: Some view the omission of a response to the conditional when

TAB-FULL:v24p97#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p97#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p97#2/r1.claim: The Great Overwhelming Calamity engulfs every lesser horror with its immense terror; it is also a name for the Day of Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v24p97#2/r1.anchor: قوله: {فإذا جاءت الطامة الكبرى} [النازعات: 34] من أسماء يوم القيامة

TAB-FULL:v24p97#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p97#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p97#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās calls it one of Resurrection's names, magnified by God as a warning to His servants.
TAB-FULL:v24p97#2/r2.anchor: من أسماء يوم القيامة، عظمه الله وحذره عباده

TAB-FULL:v24p97#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p97#2/r3.speaker: القاسم بن الوليد
TAB-FULL:v24p97#2/r3.claim: Al-Qāsim ibn al-Walīd says the people of Paradise are led to Paradise and the people of Hell to Hell.
TAB-FULL:v24p97#2/r3.anchor: قال: سيق أهل الجنة إلى الجنة، وأهل النار إلى النار

TABATABAI:79:33-41/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r2.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r2.claim: Al-Majmaʿ says al-ṭāmma is something elevated and overpowering; the word names an irresistible catastrophe.
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r2.anchor: والطامة العالية الغالبة يقال هذا أطم من هذا أي أعلى منه

TABATABAI:79:33-41/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r3.claim: The Greater Calamity is the Resurrection, which overwhelms every other calamity; the opening fa shows that it follows necessarily from the creation and governance just described.
TABATABAI:79:33-41/r3.anchor: فالمراد بالطامة الكبرى القيامة لأنها داهية تعلو وتغلب كل داهية هائلة

TABRISI:79:27-46/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:27-46/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:27-46/r4.claim: Ṭamma is something high or overpowering and, by extension, an irresistible calamity.
TABRISI:79:27-46/r4.anchor: والطامة العالية الغالبة يقال هذا أطم من هذا أي أعلى منه

TABRISI:79:27-46/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:27-46/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:27-46/r7.claim: The answer to “when the great calamity comes” is the following clause about whoever transgresses and what follows.
TABRISI:79:27-46/r7.anchor: وجواب إذا في قوله فإذا جاءت الطامة الكبرى في قوله { فأما من طغى } وما بعده

TABRISI:79:45-46/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:45-46/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:45-46/r1.claim: The great calamity is the Resurrection, which overwhelms every other disaster; Hasan identifies it as the second blast.
TABRISI:79:45-46/r1.anchor: { فإذا جاءت الطامة الكبرى } وهي القيامة لأنها تطم على كل داهية هائلة

TABRISI:79:45-46/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:45-46/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:45-46/r2.claim: Other interpretations describe it as a dense, enveloping event or the time when the people of Paradise and Hell are led to their destinations.
TABRISI:79:45-46/r2.anchor: وقيل: إن ذلك حين يساق أهل الجنة إلى الجنة وأهل النار إلى النار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197#2/r1.claim: The Great Overwhelming Event is the second trumpet blast, at which resurrection occurs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد النفخة الثانية (¬4). -وهو قول مقاتل (¬5) - التي فيها البعث

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197#2/r2.claim: He identifies the overwhelming event as the Hour; it overwhelms everything, with nothing beyond it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197#2/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي: الطامة: الساعة؛ طمت على كل شيء، فليس فوقها شيء (¬6)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197#2/r3.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197#2/r3.claim: Among Arabs, ṭamma means an unbearable calamity; he derives it from a horse exhausting itself in a run and from water filling a river.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197#2/r4.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197#2/r4.claim: The root can mean filling or burying: filling a well with earth, a flood burying a cistern, or something rising until it covers other things.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197#2/r4.anchor: قال الليث: الطم: طم البئر بالتراب، وهو الكبس، وطم السيل الركية (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197#2/r5.claim: He says the Resurrection overwhelms everything else and notes that both ṭumm and ṭamm are used.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197#2/r5.anchor: قال الفراء: هي القيامة تطم على ما سواها، ومن ثم يقال: تطم وتطم: لغتان (¬5)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197#2/r6.claim: He interprets the event as a cry that overwhelms everything.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p197#2/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج: هي الصيحة التي تطم كل شيء (¬6)

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:27-34/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:27-34/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:27-34/r6.claim: The Great Overwhelming Event means the blast of Resurrection.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:27-34/r6.anchor: { فإذا جاءت الطامة الكبرى } يعني: صيحة القيامة

ELMALILI:79:34-41/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:34-41/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:34-41/r1.claim: Tamma comes from a root meaning to overwhelm or fill; the greatest catastrophe names the resurrection, especially when Hell's and Paradise's people enter their destinations.
ELMALILI:79:34-41/r1.anchor: “Tâmme” basıp doldurmak mânasına طَمَّ’den müştak olarak üstün ve baskın güç yetmez belâ demektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:34/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:34/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:34/r1.claim: Ṭāmma names Resurrection as an overwhelming calamity so severe that it eclipses other hardships, as al-Shawkani explains.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:34/r1.anchor: Arap dilinde “dayanılamayacak kadar ağır ve başka musibetleri bastıracak ölçüde büyük musibet” anlamına gelen tâmme kelimesi burada kıyameti ifade eder

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p98/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p98/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p98/r1.claim: He groups the arrival of the great calamity with other grave or difficult events, supporting his account of Qurʾānic jāʾa as marking hardship.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p98/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p98/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p98/r2.claim: He answers the apparent counterexample by distinguishing the report of the Overwhelming, which arrives in 88:1, from the event itself arriving, as in the calamity verses.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p98/r2.anchor: والجواب: أن الذي جاء هنا هو الحديث وليس الغاشية في حين أن الذي جاء هناك هو الطَّامةُ والصاخَّة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p76/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p76/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p76/r1.claim: The coming of the great catastrophe and the blinding blast belongs to events involving great difficulty and hardship, motivating the choice of جاء.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p76/r1.anchor: وهذا كله مما فيه صعوبة ومشقة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p76/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p76/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p76/r3.claim: The contrast between أتى أمر الله and جاء أمر الله shows جاء for the harder event, which brings judgment and loss, and أتى for the easier statement.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p76/r3.anchor: المجيء الثاني أشق وأصعب لما فيه من قضاء وخسران

THALABI:v10p128/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p128/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p128/r7.claim: Al-ṭāmma al-kubrā is the Resurrection, which overwhelms every terrifying event and eclipses all else by its terror.
THALABI:v10p128/r7.anchor: فإذا جاءت الطامة الكبرى وهي القيامة سميت بذلك لأنها تطم على كل هائلة من الأمور

THALABI:v10p128/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p128/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p128/r8.claim: In Arabic, al-ṭāmma is an insurmountable event; the name is related to a horse exhausting its full effort in a run.
THALABI:v10p128/r8.anchor: والطامة عند العرب الناهية التي لا تستطاع

THALABI:v10p128/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p128/r9.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v10p128/r9.claim: Al-Hasan says the event drives the people of Paradise to Paradise and the people of Hell to Hell.
THALABI:v10p128/r9.anchor: قال الحسن: يسوق أهل الجنة إلى الجنة وأهل النار إلى النار

ELMALILI:79:27-33/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r23.claim: Al-ṭāmma al-kubrā is one of the names of the Resurrection.

ITQAN:v2p338#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p338#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p338#3/r1.claim: Al-Ghāshiya, al-ṭāmma, al-ṣākhkha, al-ḥāqqa, and al-qāriʿa are all names for the Day of Resurrection.
ITQAN:v2p338#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ الغاشية ﴾ و ﴿ الطامة ﴾ و ﴿ الصاخة ﴾ و ﴿ الحاقة ﴾ و ﴿ القارعة ﴾ من أسماء يوم القيامة

RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r1.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r1.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says the answer to the condition is omitted: the people of Hell enter Hell and the people of Paradise enter Paradise, as the following destinations indicate.
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r1.anchor: قال الواحدي : إنه محذوف على تقدير إذا جاءت الطامة دخل أهل النار النار

RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r2.speaker: مالك بن معول
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r2.claim: Mālik ibn Maʿwal glosses the Great Calamity as the moment the people of Paradise and Hell each go to their destination.
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r2.anchor: مالك بن معول في تفسير الطامة الكبرى ، قال : إنها إذا سبق أهل الجنة إلى الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, the apodosis is the statement that Hell is the abode, with a compound condition: when the calamity comes, whoever arrives as a transgressor has Hell as his home.
RAZI-FULL:v31p47#2/r3.anchor: أن جوابه قوله : { فإن الجحيم هى المأوى } وكأنه جزاء مركب على شرطين

QUSHAYRI:v3p389/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p389/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p389/r15.claim: The greatest calamity is the overwhelming catastrophe of Resurrection.

FARRA:v3p232/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p232/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p232/r8.claim: الطامة is the Resurrection, which overwhelms everything.
FARRA:v3p232/r8.anchor: وهي القيامة تطم على كل شيء

FARRA:v3p232/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p232/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p232/r9.claim: Both تطم and تطم are Arabic forms.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r2.claim: If idhā precedes a past-tense verb, the verb is shifted to the future; the past form reinforces the certainty of the event.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r2.anchor: بفعل الماضي لزيادة تحقيق ما يفيده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r3.claim: The coming of the event is metaphorical for its occurring: a timed event is pictured as a traveler arriving at a destination when its term comes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r3.anchor: والمجيء : هنا مجاز في الحصول والوقوع لأن الشيء الموقت المؤجل بأجل يشبه شخصا سائرا إلى غاية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r4.claim: Al-ṭāmma is an event that overwhelms or surpasses comparable events, rare within its class; the word derives from water covering things when it overflows.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r4.anchor: والطامة : الحادثة ، أو الوقعة التي تطم ، أي تعلو وتغلب بمعنى تفوق أمثالها من نوعها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r5.claim: The word signals severity and terror; calling it ‘the greatest’ intensifies the horrors accompanying the event.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r5.anchor: وهذا الوصف يؤذن بالشدة والهول إذ لا يقال مثله إلا في الأمور المهولة ثم بولغ في تشخيص هولها بأن وصفت ب { الكبرى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r6.claim: The great overwhelming event is the Resurrection, also described in the Qur’an as al-ṣākhkha, al-qāriʿa, and al-rājifa.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p89/r6.anchor: والمراد بالطامة الكبرى : القيامة وقد وصفت بأوصاف عديدة في القرآن مثل الصاخة والقارعة والراجفة
